title: model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen quirks + GQA/MQA tuning
author: Ethan Zhao
release_notes: Performance improvements: model-specific kernel selection and scheduling heuristics for Llama/Mistral/Qwen; KV cache fixes for MQA sharded layouts; continuous batching backpressure tuned for GQA workloads. Expect ~8-18% p99 latency reduction and 10-35% throughput uplift depending on model and sequence length.
description: Context: customer workloads show divergent performance characteristics across Llama, Mistral, and Qwen families due to attention kernel shapes, MQA/GQA query layouts, and typical sequence-length distributions. This PR implements a set of model-specific runtime optimizations: (1) kernel selection rules and micro-kernel variants for Llama and Mistral attention shapes to improve vectorization for common head/split sizes; (2) KV cache layout fixes and alignment for Qwen MQA shards to avoid extra memcpy and correctness issues at shard boundaries; (3) scheduling hints and dynamic shard placement to reduce head-of-line blocking for mixed-length workloads; (4) continuous-batching backpressure heuristic tuned for GQA-heavy traffic to reduce p99 oscillation while preserving throughput; (5) quantization profile adjustments for GQA vs MQA to avoid quality regressions while allowing lower-memory kernels. Changes are gated behind runtime flags and per-model config entries so rollout can be controlled by model tags. This PR includes unit tests for KV cache correctness across shard boundaries, micro-bench harnesses for the new kernels, and an end-to-end canary that compares baseline vs optimized runtime on the perf-canary cluster.
commits: feat(runtime): add model-specific kernel selector and micro-kernel table
fix(kv-cache): correct shard offset calculation for MQA-aligned KV stores
perf(scheduler): heuristic for dynamic shard placement and latency-aware routing
perf(batch): continuous batching backpressure threshold tuning for GQA workloads
test: add KV shard boundary unit tests and microbench harnesses
docs: update model-profiles.md with new tuning knobs

benchmarks: Llama-2-13B, seq=512: baseline p99=132ms -> optimized p99=118ms (-10.6%), throughput +18%
Mistral-7B, seq=1024: baseline p99=210ms -> optimized p99=184ms (-12.4%), throughput +22%
Qwen-7B-MQA, seq=256 (multi-query groups): baseline p99=86ms -> optimized p99=79ms (-8.1%), throughput +10%
GQA-style mixed-length workload (50/30/20 split short/med/long): p99 variability reduced from 28% to 7% across runs; average throughput +15%
Memory: MQA shard fix reduced peak host memcpy by ~30% for Qwen MQA workloads
rollout_plan: feature gated rollout: opt flag default off for existing production pools. Canary on perf-canary-3 for 48h with synthetic traffic and sampled real traffic. If canary passes (no QoL degradations and metrics within thresholds) enable for model-tags: llama-*, mistral-*, qwen-* on Dedicated batch pools, then gradual enable on Hosted region us-west-2 over 2 weeks. Rollback path: flip feature flag and use scheduler fallback policy 'legacy' to restore baseline kernels.
post_merge_actions: Create a Linear task for QA to validate customer-facing telemetry changes (ENG-2610), monitor p99 and errors for 7 days, notify on-call if p99 increases >5% or error rate >1.5x baseline.
notes: This PR consolidates multiple model-specific fixes that were causing regressions for MQA workloads and p99 instability for mixed-length GQA traffic. Most of the surface changes are hidden behind runtime flags and model profiles; ops teams can control rollout. The KV cache fix addresses a latent correctness issue discovered during a customer investigation (SUP-842).
